standingReach.note: No published Indian standing-reach data found. Derived from the heightCm ladder (Indian inter-university and India squad heights) using a reach/height ratio of ~1.31 (men) and ~1.30 (women).

sources: Pradhan K (2017) Physical Fitness and Performance Indicators of Indian Female Volleyball Players, Bhatter College J Multidisciplinary Studies 7(1) - http://www.bcjms.bhattercollege.ac.in/v7/n1/ped-en-v7-01-01.pdf
blockTouch.note: International = India squad averages (men 2019 Asian Ch. 330 cm; women U23 2015 278 cm; Asian senior women teams 262-288). University = standing reach + ~50 cm (M) / ~40 cm (W) block jump, cross-checked with Indian sub-junior national-camp girls (250 cm); levels between interpolated. Federation-listed block heights are self-reported and tend to run high.

spikeTouch.note: International = India men 2019 squad mean 343.9 cm (VNL teams 331-352) and India women U23 286 cm (Asian senior teams 287-300). University = standing reach + ~62 cm (M) / ~47 cm (W) approach jump (Japanese Div-1 university women spike jump 55 cm; Indian sub-junior national girls 255 cm); interpolated between.

proAgility.note: NCAA Division I women volleyball 5-10-5 = 4.9 +/- 0.2 s (Sports 2025), mapped to international for Indian women. Men set ~0.4 s faster, per the college men/women gap in coaching benchmarks (blog, secondary). Lower levels interpolated to the app's poor anchor.

serveVelocity.note: Sport Journal norms: FIVB World League men power jump serve 73-104 km/h, jump float 40-75; Spanish Queen's Cup women power jump 66-89, floats 40-61. International = a hard jump serve (M) / strong float-to-jump serve (W); university = float-serve speeds. Turkish league data confirm speed rises with league level.

attackVelocity.note: International men's spikes in competition averaged 22.8-25.2 m/s (82-91 km/h, ISBS); Spanish 1st-division women jump spike 71.2 km/h. These are mapped to international. Forthomme (2005) confirms 1st > 2nd division. University values estimated, and the levels between interpolated.

sources: Koley S, Singh J, Sandhu JS - Anthropometric and physiological characteristics on Indian inter-university volleyball players - https://www.redalyc.org/pdf/3010/301023489009.pdf
heightCm.note: Indian inter-university players: M 181.9 cm, W 159.7 cm (zonal). India men squad 2019: 195.3 cm, India women U23 2015: 176.3 cm (international). University set 2-3 cm below zonal; levels between interpolated.

sources: Mroczek D et al. (2014) Analysis of male volleyball players' motor activities during a top level match, J Strength Cond Res 28(8)
matchMetresPerMin.note: National-level men covered ~1250-1340 m in 30-min matches (~42-45 m/min, IMU), mapped to national. Live-ball-only rates are much higher (elite women 68.6 m/min). Polish top-league men covered ~1.2 km per 3-set match. Level differences and women's values (~8% lower) are estimated.

matchTopSpeedKmh.note: LPS data on elite/national-team women: training max speed 15.9-17.1 km/h, warm-up 13.1-15.3. National-level men exceed 15 km/h ~8 times per 30 min. Women's elite value mapped to international; men set ~1.5 km/h higher; lower levels estimated. Well below the app's football-based anchors.

matchHsrPerMin.note: Only published figure: 8.3 +/- 6.0 efforts above 15 km/h per 30-min match (national-level men). Assumed ~2-3 m per effort (~0.7 m/min) at national/international. Other levels and women estimated. Volleyball HSR is tiny, so this discriminates poorly.

matchSprintMetresPerMin.note: Null: volleyball players' top speeds are ~15-18 km/h (LPS data), so distance above 18 km/h is ~0 m/min at every level. The measure cannot separate levels in a 9 x 9 m half-court.

matchAccelPerMin.note: National-level men made 18.7 +/- 9.3 high-intensity accelerations (plus 19 decelerations >3 m/s2) per 30-min match = 0.62/min, mapped to national. Elite women made 18.5-31.8 accelerations in a 45-min warm-up. Other levels and women estimated.

sources: Kountouris P et al. (2015) Evidence for Differences in Men's and Women's Volleyball Games Based on Skills Effectiveness in Four Consecutive Olympic Tournaments, Comprehensive Psychology 4:9 - https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.2466/30.50.CP.4.9
card_attackEff.note: Olympics: successful/faulty attacks M 47.1/16.5%, W 39.6/15.0%, i.e. efficiency ~31% (M) / ~25% (W). AVC Challenge Cup 2023 kill% M 48.5-56.9, W 40.3-49.2. Directorate Elite (35/30) mapped to international, which is ambitious vs Olympic averages. University kept at the approved 25/20.

card_receptionPos.note: Published elite 'excellent' reception is 58.8-60.4% (Olympics) and 'precise' is 53.5-60.2% (AVC Challenge Cup 2023). Both count perfect+good, not perfect-only as in the app formula, so they are not directly comparable. Kept the approved University 30, mapped Elite 40 to international, and interpolated.

card_serveAce.note: Null (rule 4): ace % depends on the opponent's reception. International rates are at or below the approved University target of 5: Olympics M 5.0%, W 4.5%; AVC Challenge Cup 2023 M 2.9-5.3%, W 3.0-3.8%. If a single target is needed, keep the directorate's 5 (University) / 6 (Elite) as flat targets.

card_serveFault.note: Men null (rule 4): elite men serve riskier jump serves and fault more (Olympics 15.2%, AVC 14.4-15.5%; directorate Elite 20 is worse than University 15). Women fault less at higher levels (Olympics 8.7%, AVC 6.4-7.0%), so the approved Elite 10 was mapped to national and international set to 8.5.

card_setEff.note: No published set-efficiency norms using the (+ minus -)/attempts formula were found. Kept the approved University 30, mapped Elite 45 to international, and interpolated evenly.

card_digEff.note: No published dig-efficiency norms using this formula were found. Kept the approved University 5, mapped Elite 20 to international, and interpolated evenly.

card_blockPerSet.note: The only published figure is Olympic block success (18.6% M, 17% W); no per-player per-set norms were found. Kept the approved University 0.3, mapped Elite 0.6 to international, and interpolated. Middle blockers will sit well above these all-position values.
